conviction_note: The baseline's 1.89% expected move is unusable - it flags cadence_implausible and disowns its own history - and the corpus supplies a better anchor: a third-party read that options implied about 3.5% against a 7.1% median over the past eight quarters, so the market is pricing half the real move into the first print that has to quantify a roughly RMB 5.2bn antitrust penalty and address the take-rate consequences of a monopoly finding; slightly negative, and small because the stock is already 44.48% below its high and near book value.

findings.finding: Trip.com was hit with a penalty of nearly RMB 5.2bn together with a monopoly finding that, in the corpus's own words, 'raises the probability of weaker take rates, higher compliance costs' - and this is the first print that has to book the charge and guide take rates around it, while pre-print options implied only about a 3.5% move ($1.61) against a 7.1% median over the past eight quarters, with call volume leading puts 8:3.

findings.why_not_priced: The mispricing is in the size, not just the sign. A 3.5% implied move against a 7.1% eight-quarter realised median means the option market is charging half of what this name actually does on prints, and it is doing so into the single most consequential disclosure of the year - the quarter in which a multi-billion-renminbi penalty lands and management has to say what a monopoly determination does to take rates. Nothing in this 38-item capture engages with that: there is no sell-side note, no consensus revenue figure and no company document, and the only substantive commentary is a valuation case (6.9x TTM earnings, $17 a share of cash, book value $36 against a $43.84 price) that treats the penalty as a one-off. Call volume leading puts 8:3 says the positioning is on the recovery side. I sign it negative but small because the price has already absorbed a 44.48% drawdown to within 22% of book, which is a real floor, and because international bookings growing 65-90% is a genuine offset.

baseline_tension: It sits with the run-up, which is -4.65% over five days and -6.40% over twenty, and with the reaction history's direction (two up out of eight) while flatly contradicting its magnitude: the baseline says 1.89% and the corpus says the eight-quarter median is 7.1%. I have used the corpus figure.
corpus_limits: This is a bmo print, so per the sweep rule I excluded the final snapshot snapshots/20260902T150722Z.json (started 2026-09-02T15:07:22Z, after a pre-open release) and did not open its stored body. The baseline is unusable for magnitude by its own admission - the eight matched 6-Ks are on a 17-day cadence and are most likely monthly operational updates, not prints. No option chain or skew, so the 3.5% implied move and the 8:3 call-put ratio are a third-party report relayed on StockTwits rather than measured. No news documents and no stored filing bodies. The penalty figure, the monopoly finding, the valuation anchors and the booking growth are all second-hand.
